note: Cases mirror the unit tests of traits/sigil_context.rs: payload_in_tick_is_rejected, payload_in_effect_is_allowed, entity_binding_is_allowed_in_all_contexts, pascalcase_entity_bindings_skip_sigil_check, out_of_scope_item_gets_the_hoist_diagnostic_not_the_sigil_list, item_in_scope_is_still_accepted, lambda_locals_are_skipped, let_locals_are_valid_roots_in_body, let_value_exprs_see_prior_bindings_only (both halves) and unknown_sigil_root_in_guard_is_rejected, plus fn parameter lists, the collection source argument, non-collection operators, object values and finding order. The sigil lists are the installed binding-rules.json fed as FACTS_HEARD; the operator rows are fed as SHAPES_HEARD (a collection or std-array operator of two or more arguments introduces item and index). Differences: none in code, path or message. The compiler's binding validator (binding.rs) is retired: this rule is the one owner of both codes. Added for the retirement of the compiler's binding.rs (G-ORB-579): an @ensures reads the guard sigils plus the rule's `ensuresSigils` knob (@fromEntity), a state's @holds and an entity or auxiliary entity invariant read the guard sigils; each reports the same code at the Rust path (a finding names its own context in the message).

findings.message: Binding @payload is not allowed in tick context. Allowed sigils: entity, state, now, config, user
Binding @item is not in scope here — @item / @index are bound only inside a collection callback (array/map, array/filter, …).
findings.suggestion: Under `children:` the collection callback must use the EXPLICIT lambda form — `(array/map <collection> (fn (item) <node>))`. The implicit shorthand `(array/map <collection> { … })` is not recognised there, so its body is not treated as a lambda and @item never comes into scope. Both a raw `type:` object and a JSX element are valid as <node>.
